haiku-low.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If the order has not claimed it by then, the stock goes back on sale.
haiku-low.q2: Reserved before payment is requested. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is requested, and the customer is told which items.
haiku-low.q3: Retries reuse the order id as idempotency key, so the provider treats them as the same request and the customer is never charged twice.
haiku-low.q4: Order is cancelled as out of stock and the customer emailed. Payment refunds the full amount, retried until the provider confirms.
haiku-low.q5: Cart empties only when Order publishes OrderConfirmed, handled by Cart. If checkout fails for any reason, the cart stays exactly as it was.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service calls Inventory and Payment and reacts to their events. It stores each order's status and snapshot.
haiku-low.q7: Provider calls Payment's webhook (seconds to 30 minutes). Payment stores the new webhook id, then publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker for Order.
haiku-low.q8: Payment checks each webhook id against ids already stored; a repeat is ignored, so nothing is processed twice.
haiku-low.q9: Order cancels, and the OrderCancelled event tells Inventory to release the hold. If the hold already lapsed, there is nothing to release.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory tries to claim the hold, or re-reserve all lines if lapsed. Success confirms the order; failure cancels it and refunds in full.
haiku-low.q11: It stays REQUESTED and is retried with backoff; a person is alerted after repeated failures. Pending refunds are tracked in Payment's refund records.
haiku-low.q12: Cart empties itself on the OrderConfirmed event, published by Order when it marks the order CONFIRMED. The Cart service does it.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If the order hasn't claimed it by then, the stock goes back on sale (the hold lapses).
sonnet.q2: Reserved before charging. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is requested, the order is cancelled, the customer is told which items are short, and the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q3: Every charge request carries the order id as its idempotency key, so the provider treats a retry as the same request.
sonnet.q4: The customer is fully refunded and the order is marked CANCELLED as out of stock; the customer is emailed and OrderCancelled is published.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only when the OrderConfirmed event is published (order confirmed). If checkout fails, the cart stays exactly as it was.
sonnet.q6: NOT STATED as a single component. The document describes Order (calling Inventory/Payment, reacting to events) and broker events driving steps, but names no single orchestrator. The order's status (PENDING, CONFIRMED, CANCELLED) is stored by the Order service.
sonnet.q7: The provider calls Payment's webhook; Payment dedupes it, stores the id, and publishes a PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined event on the broker, which Order reacts to.
sonnet.q8: Payment checks the webhook id against the webhook ids it has stored; a repeat is ignored, a new one is stored and processed.
sonnet.q9: Order cancels the order, and the OrderCancelled event tells Inventory to release the hold. If the hold has already lapsed, there is nothing to release.
sonnet.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim the hold; if lapsed, Inventory tries to reserve all lines again, all or nothing. If that works the order is confirmed; if not (stock sold to someone else) the order is cancelled and fully refunded.
sonnet.q11: The refund stays REQUESTED, is retried later with backoff, and a person is alerted after repeated failures. It is tracked in Payment's database as a refund record saved before sending, marked DONE only when the provider confirms.
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event published by Order; the Cart service empties the cart on that event.
